verdicts_or_reports.expected: The displayed https://example.com/guide note link is detected and tapping it opens the link (or an app chooser).
verdicts_or_reports.observed: The note is rendered as plain text. Tapping the URL area twice opens the Read docs task editor instead of opening the link.
steps: On My Tasks, use no grouping so Read docs and its note are visible.
Tap the https://example.com/guide text in the Read docs note.
Observe that the task editor opens; save without changes to return to the list.
Tap the same URL text again and observe the task editor opens again.

verdicts_or_reports.expected: In the task list's displayed note, https://example.com/guide is recognized as a web link and shown/handled as a link.
verdicts_or_reports.observed: The URL is displayed in the same plain gray note style as ordinary text, with no link styling. Tapping the URL area opens the task editor instead of the web link.
steps: Open My Tasks with the provided Read docs task.
Set grouping to By due date so the No due date section is visible.
Inspect the displayed Read docs note: the URL is plain gray text with no link styling.
Tap the URL text; the task editor opens instead of a link destination or chooser.

verdicts_or_reports.expected: The four existing tasks should remain visible under the Default list group.
verdicts_or_reports.observed: Selecting List grouping removes all tasks and shows the empty-state message even though switching to None restores the same tasks.
steps: Open the My Tasks list containing Buy milk, Pack for trip, Pay rent, and Read docs.
Open Sort, choose Grouping, then choose List.
Observe the empty-state message.
Switch grouping to None and verify the tasks return.
Choose List again and observe the same empty state.

verdicts_or_reports.expected: With Sorting set to By title · Descending and Grouping set to None, parent tasks should appear in reverse alphabetical order: Read docs, Pay rent, Pack for trip, Buy milk.
verdicts_or_reports.observed: The sort sheet shows By title · Descending, but the list remains in ascending order with Buy milk first and Read docs last.
steps: Open Sort and set Grouping to None.
Set Sorting to By title and close the sheet; verify the parent tasks appear ascending.
Reopen Sort, tap the Sorting direction control to change Ascending to Descending, and close the sheet.
Observe that the list remains Buy milk, Pack for trip, Pay rent, Read docs instead of reversing.
Reopen Sort and verify it still shows By title · Descending.

verdicts_or_reports.expected: With Subtasks set to By title · Descending, the trip's subtasks should show Print tickets before Charge phone.
verdicts_or_reports.observed: The sort sheet retains By title · Descending, but the subtasks remain in ascending order: Charge phone appears before Print tickets.
steps: Open Sort and set Grouping to None.
Set Sorting to By title · Ascending.
Set Subtasks to By title · Descending and close the sheet.
Open Pack for trip and observe Charge phone still appears before Print tickets.
Reopen Sort and verify Subtasks still shows By title · Descending.
